Code Unpacked · Walkthrough

Vue Vapor · Reviewing a new renderer across 303 files

A guided architecture review with 12 deep dives, source excerpts, ownership invariants and explicit gaps.

Overview · Overview

Purpose

Review 303 changed files through one source-backed path: SFC opt-in → template AST → Vapor IR → generated DOM program → scoped reactive blocks. Then examine component semantics, two renderer adapters, hydration and shared compatibility changes. Proposed extensions and review priorities are explicitly labeled.

Overview · Overview

Review order

1. 01 · From template AST to DOM program: Review order: compile.ts → IR types → TransformContext → block/operation generators → matching runtime helpers. 2. 01 · From template AST to DOM program: Invariant: static template shape, referenced node IDs and emitted operations must describe the same DOM tree; every new operation needs a generator/runtime counterpart. 3. 02 · Static templates, dynamic operations and expressions: Invariant: child/next/nthChild addressing must account for non-template children and insertion anchors. 4. 02 · Static templates, dynamic operations and expressions: Review expression scope, ref unwrapping, assignment targets and temporary caching together with generated effects; output snapshots alone do not prove runtime semantics. 5. 03 · Conditions, keyed lists and insertion ownership: Invariant: removing or replacing a branch stops its effects as well as removing DOM; equal branch keys preserve the current branch. 6. 03 · Conditions, keyed lists and insertion ownership: Audit keyed/unkeyed identity, empty-list removal and compiler-only fast flags together. FAST_REMOVE is justified only for the generated topology. 7. 04 · Reactive scheduling and scope restoration: Invariant: instance and active scope are restored after nested work; scope.stop must detach all effects and cleanup callbacks. 8. 04 · Reactive scheduling and scope restoration: Check initial synchronous execution, batched nextTick updates, update-hook grouping, error paths and recursive-update limits separately; renderEffect explicitly retains a recurse-handling TODO. 9. 05 · Component creation, getter props and fallthrough: Invariant: declared props, emit listeners and fallthrough attrs remain distinct even when names are dynamic or camelized. 10. 05 · Component creation, getter props and fallthrough: Check source precedence, default factories, class/style merging and single-root fallthrough; an exposed props proxy is not evidence of eager value storage. 11. 06 · Slots, emits, template refs and directives: Invariant: resolving the same slot should preserve its bound identity, while changed slots/fallbacks dispose old content. 12. 06 · Slots, emits, template refs and directives: Treat custom Vapor directives as function-based contracts with optional disposal, not as the VDOM directive-hook object API; inspect dynamic refs and their cleanup TODOs. 13. 07 · DOM setters and event strategy: Invariant: removed dynamic keys are cleared and changing effect-bound listeners do not accumulate registrations. 14. 07 · DOM setters and event strategy: Review HTML assignment as raw DOM behavior, property-versus-attribute classification, boolean/value edge cases and event modifiers; the dynamic setter has explicit SVG and checkbox TODOs. 15. 08 · SFC opt-in and compiler selection: Invariant: parse-time mode, script marker, template backend and runtime exports must agree; SSR selection takes precedence over the Vapor client compiler. 16. 08 · SFC opt-in and compiler selection: Review both JavaScript and TypeScript component exports, inline templates and non-inline development output. 17. 09 · Two renderers, two adapter directions: Invariant: a component is mounted, moved and unmounted by the same owning renderer/adaptor; anchors remain stable across updates. 18. 09 · Two renderers, two adapter directions: Review both directions and both slot directions independently. TODO unit suites and a specific end-to-end example do not establish universal interop parity. 19. 10 · Hydration adopts existing DOM: Invariant: the hydration cursor advances with the same static-template/fragment structure expected by generated navigation. 20. 10 · Hydration adopts existing DOM: Exercise empty/nested fragments, prepend anchors, branch/list shape changes and mismatches; warnings with TODO recovery are not a full recovery guarantee. 21. 11 · Shared runtime APIs and packaging: Review shared apiCreateApp, GenericComponentInstance consumers, public/internal exports, HMR and renderer changes as compatibility-sensitive code. 22. 11 · Shared runtime APIs and packaging: Treat benchmarks as measurement machinery and fixtures, not evidence of a universal speed or size claim; this bundle does not execute Vue’s benchmark/test suite. 23. 12 · Review invariants, tests and extension seams: Proposed review order: compiler-pipeline → transform-codegen → structural-blocks → reactivity-lifecycle → components-props → slots/events/DOM → SFC → interop/hydration → shared integration. 24. 12 · Review invariants, tests and extension seams: Test interpretation: snapshots show emitted shape; runtime tests show selected scenarios; e2e fixtures show a concrete full flow; TODO suites remain gaps.

Overview · Overview

Extension guidance

Proposed extension · 01 · From template AST to DOM program: Add a syntax feature through the node/directive transform preset, a typed IR operation when needed, its generator and a runtime helper; test both emitted code and behavior. Proposed extension · 02 · Static templates, dynamic operations and expressions: Extend expression handling in generators/expression.ts with binding/scope cases and targeted transform snapshots, then exercise the resulting helpers in runtime tests. Proposed extension · 03 · Conditions, keyed lists and insertion ownership: Add structural behavior at the transform/IR/generator boundary and pair it with scope-cleanup, reorder and nested-block runtime tests. Proposed extension · 04 · Reactive scheduling and scope restoration: Use renderEffect for reactive DOM work and the owning EffectScope for teardown; add tests that mutate after removal and verify current instance/scope inside scheduled reruns. Proposed extension · 05 · Component creation, getter props and fallthrough: Extend props semantics in the getter/normalization layer and compiler raw-props generation together; preserve declared-prop/attr/emits separation and test source precedence. Proposed extension · 06 · Slots, emits, template refs and directives: Extend slot selection in transform and runtime resolution together; for directives return a cleanup function and verify disposal in branches and lists. Proposed extension · 07 · DOM setters and event strategy: Add DOM semantics through the specialized generator/helper seam and tests for attr/prop coercion, listener cleanup, fallthrough and form-control behavior. Proposed extension · 08 · SFC opt-in and compiler selection: Add SFC integration options at the descriptor/compileScript/compileTemplate boundary and test both TS/JS plus inline/non-inline output and SSR selection. Proposed extension · 09 · Two renderers, two adapter directions: Extend interop through VaporInteropInterface and the plugin adapters, preserving native props/slot semantics on each side; add focused tests before expanding supported combinations. Proposed extension · 10 · Hydration adopts existing DOM: Improve mismatch diagnostics/recovery in hydration adoption and cursor location, paired with compiler-generated shape fixtures and retained DOM identity assertions. Proposed extension · 11 · Shared runtime APIs and packaging: Prefer existing generic runtime seams for shared behavior; when adding exports, verify enabled/trimmed build surfaces and both renderer test configurations. Proposed extension · 12 · Review invariants, tests and extension seams: For a new feature, write a transform/generator expectation plus a runtime ownership/timing test and, when crossing renderers, an end-to-end adapter test. Keep unsupported combinations explicit.

01 · From template AST to DOM program · Deep dive

One parser, a different lowering contract

compile() accepts a string or existing RootNode, parses strings with compiler-dom, combines built-in and supplied transforms, then calls transform() followed by generate(). The important architectural change is the intermediate representation: this is a parallel backend with its own operations, not a switch that makes the existing VNode code generator silently emit DOM code. Follow that explicit handoff when reviewing scope.

01 · From template AST to DOM program · Deep dive

Read the IR as a plan, not emitted JavaScript

RootIRNode owns deduplicated template strings and component/directive assets. A BlockIRNode separates creation-time operations, reactive effects, dynamic node information and return nodes. DynamicFlag records whether a node needs a variable, is outside a static template, or needs insertion. These flags connect structural transforms to later DOM navigation; confusing template index with node identity can generate valid-looking code for the wrong node.

01 · From template AST to DOM program · Deep dive

Transform ordering is part of the API

The preset runs once, structural directives, slots and refs before element/text/children handling. transformNode runs entry transforms in order and exit callbacks in reverse; transforms may replace or remove context.node. User node transforms append to the preset, while user directive transforms override the directive map. A plugin must respect this ordering and restore block state when its exit callback runs.

02 · Static templates, dynamic operations and expressions · Deep dive

Static HTML is a reusable factory

TransformContext deduplicates template strings. genTemplates emits module-level template(...) factories; the runtime parses element HTML once for a factory, clones its root for each invocation, and uses a text-node fast path. A root marker supports attribute fallthrough. During hydration the same factory adopts an existing node instead of cloning. Static-template caching therefore does not mean one DOM node is shared across component instances.

02 · Static templates, dynamic operations and expressions · Deep dive

Find nodes before changing the tree

transformChildren tracks dynamic children outside the template and places explicit anchors where needed. genChildren compensates its DOM child index for NON_TEMPLATE entries and reuses child/next/nthChild paths. genBlockContent first emits nodes and navigation references, then operations, then effects. Review this ordering with mixed static elements, components, conditionals and lists; an insertion performed too early can invalidate a later positional lookup.

02 · Static templates, dynamic operations and expressions · Deep dive

Creation operations and effects have different lifetimes

registerEffect filters constant expressions and promotes v-once or statically known work into ordinary block operations. genEffects processes the remaining expressions and wraps emitted operations in renderEffect. Several operations can share that wrapper; do not assume each interpolation creates a distinct ReactiveEffect. The review invariant is dependency/lifetime correctness, not a one-to-one mapping between source directives and effect objects.

Bindings determine reads and writes

genExpression distinguishes literal/static expressions, simple identifiers and walked AST expressions. genIdentifier consults local identifier mappings and SFC binding metadata, so loop/slot aliases, setup refs, maybe-refs and props require different access or assignment forms. Generated helper imports come from CodegenContext.helper usage. Follow a binding from SFC metadata through expression generation rather than checking only the final identifier spelling.

03 · Conditions, keyed lists and insertion ownership · Deep dive

Branches own effect scopes

The v-if transform creates block IR and records positive/negative branches. createIf either evaluates once or installs a render effect that selects a BlockFn. DynamicFragment.update returns immediately for an unchanged key; otherwise it pauses tracking, stops the old scope, removes old nodes, runs the new branch in a fresh scope and inserts before its retained anchor. Branch factories should not re-run merely because a value used inside the current branch changes.

Insertion state is a handoff

For block operations, codegen emits setInsertionState(parent, anchor). createIf, createFor, createComponent and createSlot save that state and either reset it or locate a hydration node before doing nested work. This avoids threading parent/anchor arguments through every generated expression, but makes nesting and reset order a critical invariant. A keyed list reuses blocks, not virtual nodes

createFor normalizes the source and retains ForBlock objects holding nodes, an optional scope and shallow item/key/index refs. The keyed path matches keys, removes missing blocks, tracks old positions and computes getSequence when movement is detected; a reverse walk then mounts or moves using the next block as anchor. A reused block receives new ref values so its own effects update. Unkeyed lists instead reuse by position.

Fast paths carry proof obligations

The transform marks an only-child list, component items and once/static sources. Runtime flags can clear a container with textContent, skip the outer item scope for components, or render the list once. These are observable lifetime choices, not cosmetic optimizations. When extending flags, check that sibling DOM is preserved, component scopes still unmount, and removed item subscriptions cannot fire against detached nodes.

04 · Reactive scheduling and scope restoration · Deep dive

Immediate setup, scheduled updates

renderEffect creates a ReactiveEffect, assigns a scheduler that queues a job, and runs it immediately. The job reruns only when dirty and carries instance UID/metadata when a component exists. Tests show a ref mutation leaves the old observed value until nextTick, while the initial value is visible immediately. Treat this timing as a boundary when comparing generated DOM behavior with user watches and lifecycle hooks.

One update cycle can contain several effects

The wrapper remembers whether update hooks existed when renderEffect was created. 05 · Component creation, getter props and fallthrough · Deep dive

A component instance owns its resources

createComponent preserves insertion state, can dispatch a non-Vapor child through an installed adapter, creates the instance, makes it current, pauses tracking and invokes setup with error handling. The instance owns a detached EffectScope and inherits app context/provides/IDs. Production setup normally yields a Block; the development path can proxy setup state and invoke a separate render function for tooling/HMR.

05 · Component creation, getter props and fallthrough · Deep dive

Raw props are getters and ordered sources

RawProps maps names to zero-argument getters; its dollar field holds dynamic object sources or getter maps. The props proxy recognizes declared, camelized keys, searches dynamic sources from last to first, and calls resolvePropValue for defaults and casts. Reads invoke the current source, so consumers establish dependencies through access. This differs from eagerly copying a plain props object each parent render.

05 · Component creation, getter props and fallthrough · Deep dive

Attrs have their own merging rules

Attr handlers filter declared props and emit listeners. Ordinary dynamic values use the later source; class and style merge across sources. Single-root children can receive parent attrs as another dynamic source, and root DOM setters coordinate fallthrough with separate caches. Review these paths together: a listener declared in emits must not also become a native DOM listener and fire twice.

05 · Component creation, getter props and fallthrough · Deep dive

Mounting and teardown cross two timelines

mountComponent calls beforeMount, inserts the block, queues mounted and marks the instance mounted. unmountComponent calls beforeUnmount, stops the instance scope, queues unmounted, marks it unmounted and optionally removes DOM. Scope disposal registers component teardown, making ownership as important as insertion. Template refs and app mount flushing add post-flush work; synchronous DOM removal alone is not the complete lifecycle.

Slot identity prevents unnecessary reconstruction

getSlot searches dynamic slot sources before static entries. createSlot wraps raw slot props in a proxy and, for a native Vapor slot, caches slot._bound so DynamicFragment sees a stable function for the same slot. A dynamic name or dollar slot sources install a renderEffect; a static outlet can render once. Fallback is installed when the selected block is invalid or no slot resolves.

withVaporDirectives invokes a function with node, value getter, argument and modifiers, registering a returned cleanup with onScopeDispose. v-model uses reusable runtime-dom model initialization/update helpers with render effects after mount. v-show follows the resolved root/block and updates display. A Vapor child in a VDOM tree

The adapter inserts a self-anchor, makes the VDOM parent current, wraps vnode props and children in shallow refs, creates the Vapor instance and mounts its block before the anchor. No VNode subtree is invented for the Vapor component internals.

Hydration changes factory and insertion behavior

createVaporSSRApp uses withHydration around createComponent and mountComponent. withHydration enables adoption functions, sets an initial prepend insertion state and clears global hydration state afterward. template() uses currentHydrationNode and adoptTemplate instead of cloning; insert() skips direct Node insertion while hydrating. This reuses the DOM program against server-rendered nodes rather than diffing a new virtual tree.

The integration surface is wider than two packages

Runtime-core generalizes instance/app types and exports helpers reused by Vapor; runtime-dom exposes model and property helpers; shared utilities include DOM classification and getSequence. Follow one feature through all layers

Start with one interpolation or keyed branch: locate its transform, IR operation, generator and runtime helper, then its test.
